chunks: And whatever is narrated from Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari, I have narrated it from my father, and from Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, and from Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil - may Allah be pleased with them - from Abdullah ibn Jafar ibn Jami' Al-Himyari.

key_terms.أبي: My father (referring to the narrator's father, a key scholar)
key_terms.عبد الله بن جعفر الحميري: Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari, a companion of the Imams
key_terms.عبد الله بن جعفر بن جامع الحميري: Abdullah ibn Jafar ibn Jami' Al-Himyari, the ultimate source in this chain
key_terms.محمد بن الحسن: Muhammad ibn Al-Hasan, a prominent narrator
key_terms.محمد بن موسى بن المتوكل: Muhammad ibn Musa ibn Al-Mutawakkil, a narrator

ai.seo_question: Who is the original source of the narrations from Abdullah ibn Jafar Al-Himyari?
ai.summary: This passage highlights the rigorous chain of transmission (isnad) in Shia scholarship, linking Shaykh al-Saduq directly to Abdullah ibn Jafar al-Himyari through his father and other key narrators like Muhammad ibn al-Hasan. By explicitly naming these intermediaries, the text underscores the reliability and continuity of the scholarly lineage, a critical element in validating hadith authenticity within the Ja'fari tradition.
